definitions.explanation: a cultivated area for growing crops or raising livestock, often implying a larger or more organized operation than a simple field

examples.japanese: コーヒー{農園|のうえん}を{見学|けんがく}した。
{祖父|そふ}は{小|ちい}さな{農園|のうえん}で{野菜|やさい}を{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: My grandfather grows vegetables on a small farm.

examples.japanese: {市民|しみん}{農園|のうえん}を{借|か}りて、{週末|しゅうまつ}に{家族|かぞく}で{農作業|のうさぎょう}を{楽|たの}しんでいる。
examples.english: We rent a community garden plot and enjoy farming as a family on weekends.

notes:
Covers a range from large commercial plantations (coffee, tea, fruit) to small community garden plots. In modern urban Japan, {市民|しみん}{農園|のうえん} (community garden/allotment) is a popular concept where city dwellers can rent small plots.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {市民|しみん}{農園|のうえん}: community garden, allotment
- {観光|かんこう}{農園|のうえん}: tourist farm (pick-your-own)
- {果樹|かじゅ}{農園|のうえん}: fruit farm/orchard
- {農園|のうえん}{経営|けいえい}: farm management
- {貸|か}し{農園|のうえん}: rental garden plot

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {農場|のうじょう}: farm — more general, often larger scale or livestock-oriented
- {畑|はたけ}: field, vegetable garden — a specific cultivated plot, smaller scale
- {牧場|ぼくじょう}: ranch, pasture — specifically for livestock
- {果樹園|かじゅえん}: orchard — specifically for fruit trees

ETYMOLOGY:
{農|のう} (agriculture) + {園|えん} (garden, park). The {園|えん} component gives it a slightly more cultivated or managed nuance than {農場|のうじょう}.
